record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let M be a closed Riemannian manifold, meaning compact and without boundary. Must M contain a connected closed geodesic multinet, that is, a finite connected immersed multigraph in M whose edges are non-constant geodesic segments between vertices, may intersect or self-intersect, and carry positive integer multiplicities, such that the multiplicity-weighted sum of outgoing unit tangent vectors at every vertex is zero, and such that the multinet contains no non-trivial periodic geodesic?

evidence.quote: Geodesic multinets are defined in the same way with the two following distinctions: 1) Edges are allowed to intersect and self-intersect; 2) Each edge is endowed with a positive integer multiplicity;
Problem 2.0.1. Is it true that each closed Riemannian manifold contains a closed geodesic multinet not containing a non-trivial periodic geodesic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold (compact and without boundary). A closed geodesic multinet in $M$ is a finite connected immersed multigraph in $M$ such that:
(i) each edge is a non-constant geodesic segment joining two vertices (possibly the same vertex), and edges are permitted to intersect each other and to self-intersect;
(ii) each edge $e$ carries a positive integer multiplicity $m(e) \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$;
(iii) at every vertex $v$, the balancing condition
$$\sum_{e \ni v} m(e)\, \tau_e(v) \;=\; 0$$
holds, where the sum is over all edges $e$ incident to $v$ (each loop counted with both its endpoints) and $\tau_e(v)$ is the unit tangent vector to $e$ at $v$ pointing into $e$.

A non-trivial periodic geodesic in the multinet is a closed geodesic curve in $M$ traced out as a non-trivial cycle in the multigraph using its geodesic edges.

Question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold $M$ contain a closed geodesic multinet that does not contain any non-trivial periodic geodesic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on geodesic nets. Recent work (2024–2025) by Nabutovsky, Parsch, and others has produced stationary geodesic nets that are not closed geodesics and established generic density of such nets, but no general resolution of the multinet existence question for every closed Riemannian manifold has been reported. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey paper listing this question as Problem 2.0.1 among open problems on geodesic nets.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an explicit open question.

status_evidence.title: Generic density of stationary geodesic nets that are not closed geodesics
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results guarantee the existence of stationary geodesic nets containing no closed geodesics on an open set of metrics on a closed manifold; confirms a Nabutovsky–Parsch conjecture on generic density.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for generic metrics, but no general solution for all closed Riemannian manifolds is reported.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Continuing work on balanced/stationary geodesic nets, indicating ongoing research without resolution of the general multinet existence question.
status_evidence.claim: Research on the topic remains active without a complete answer.
